I'll start by looking at the repo state before changing anything. "Clean up" could mean several different things, and I don't want to make edits you didn't ask for.

TOOL: git status --short && echo "---" && git log --oneline -n 10 && echo "---" && git stash list && echo "---" && git branch -vv && echo "---" && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | sed 's|^\./||' | sort | head -n 200
